title: Analyzers
description: Reactor ships a set of Roslyn analyzers that catch common mistakes while you write code: a hook inside an if, a list item with no key, a hard-coded color, an icon button with no name for screen readers. Each rule has an ID that starts with REACTOR. Many rules also have a code fix that rewrites the code for you.

---
title: "Analyzers"
description: "Reactor ships a set of Roslyn analyzers that catch common mistakes while you write code: a hook inside an if, a list item with no key, a hard-coded color, an icon button with no name for screen readers. Each rule has an ID that starts with REACTOR. Many rules also have a code fix that rewrites the code for you."
---

You don't install anything extra. The analyzers are inside the
`Microsoft.UI.Reactor` NuGet package, in its `analyzers/dotnet/cs` folder,
so every project that references the package runs them.

## Where the warnings show up [#where-the-warnings-show-up]

![Your code is checked by the REACTOR analyzers. The results show up in three places: the editor, the dotnet build output, and mur check.](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/images/analyzers/two-surfaces.svg)

- **In the editor.** Visual Studio and VS Code with the C# extension show
  a squiggle while you type. Press `Ctrl+.` on the squiggle to see the code
  fix, if the rule has one.
- **In the build.** `dotnet build` and CI print the same warnings and
  errors.
- **In `mur check`.** It runs the build and prints each diagnostic on one
  line, with a hint on how to fix it. See [`mur check`](#mur-check).

## Change the severity [#change-the-severity]

Set the severity of one rule in an `.editorconfig` file at the root of your
project or solution:

```ini
[*.cs]
# Fail the build when a hook is called conditionally.
dotnet_diagnostic.REACTOR_HOOKS_001.severity = error

# Turn off one rule.
dotnet_diagnostic.REACTOR_DSL_004.severity = none

# Raise every rule in one category.
dotnet_analyzer_diagnostic.category-Reactor.Hooks.severity = error
```

The values are `error`, `warning`, `suggestion`, `silent`, and `none`. The
category names are in the [table](#all-rules).

To turn off a rule for one line, wrap the line in
`#pragma warning disable REACTOR_DSL_004` and
`#pragma warning restore REACTOR_DSL_004`. To make every warning fail the
build, set `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` in the
project file.

## Examples [#examples]

Each example shows code that a rule flags, and the code that fixes it.
[Rules of Reactor](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/get-started/rules-of-reactor) explains why these rules exist.

**Hooks must run on every render.** This code calls `UseState` only when
`ShouldCount` is true, so `REACTOR_HOOKS_001` fires:

```csharp
// Wrong: REACTOR_HOOKS_001
if (ShouldCount)
{
    var (count, _) = UseState(0);
    return TextBlock($"Count: {count}");
}
return TextBlock("No counter.");
```

Call the hook every time, and move the condition into the output:

```csharp
class HookOrderGood : Component
{
    public bool ShouldCount;

    public override Element Render()
    {
        // Hook always runs; the conditional moves into the render output.
        var (count, _) = UseState(0);
        return ShouldCount
            ? TextBlock($"Count: {count}")
            : TextBlock("No counter.");
    }
}
```

**Items in a dynamic list need a key.** Without `.WithKey`, the reconciler
matches rows by position. `REACTOR_DSL_001` fires:

```csharp
// Wrong: REACTOR_DSL_001
Items.Select(i => TextBox(i.Title, title => Rename(i, title))).ToArray()
```

Key each row by a stable ID. The code fix adds the `.WithKey(...)` call:

```csharp
class TodoListGood : Component
{
    public TodoItem[] Items = System.Array.Empty<TodoItem>();

    public override Element Render() => VStack(4,
        Items.Select(i =>
            TextBox(i.Title, title => Rename(i, title), header: i.Id.ToString())
                .WithKey(i.Id.ToString())                  // stable identity
        ).ToArray()
    );

    void Rename(TodoItem item, string title)
    {
        var index = System.Array.IndexOf(Items, item);
        if (index >= 0)
            Items[index] = item with { Title = title };
    }
}
```

**Use theme tokens, not hard-coded colors.** A hex color does not follow
light, dark, or high-contrast themes. `REACTOR_THEME_001` fires and
suggests a token:

```csharp
// Wrong: REACTOR_THEME_001
Button("Save", () => { }).Background("#0078D4");
```

The code fix replaces the color with the token:

```csharp
// Do:
Button("Save", () => { }).Background(Theme.Accent);
```

## mur check [#mur-check]

[`mur check`](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/tools/mur-cli#check-your-code) runs `dotnet build`, so it sees
every diagnostic the analyzers report. It does not run a second copy of the
rules. It changes how the results are shown:

- In the default mode, it prints errors and `REACTOR_` warnings. It hides
  info-level rules and most other warnings, including `REACTOR0050`, whose ID
  has no underscore. `--final` prints everything. `--strict` ranks every
  warning as an error, so all warnings print.
- For 11 rules it adds a pointer to the skill section that explains the fix:
  `REACTOR_HOOKS_001`, `REACTOR_HOOKS_004`, `REACTOR_HOOKS_005`,
  `REACTOR_HOOKS_006`, `REACTOR_HOOKS_009`, `REACTOR_THEME_001`,
  `REACTOR_THEME_002`, `REACTOR_A11Y_001`, `REACTOR_DSL_001`,
  `REACTOR_DOCK_001`, and `REACTOR_ITEMS_002`.
- For compiler errors such as `CS0103` and `CS1061`, it suggests the Reactor
  name you probably meant (`→ try: ...`). These suggestions cover mistakes
  that the analyzers can't see, because the code does not compile.
- It has seven rules of its own for common mistakes. One of them mirrors
  `REACTOR_DYM_006` and prints the hex value for an unknown color name.

The
[`mur check` design notes](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/blob/main/docs/reference/mur-check-did-you-mean.md)
describe each tier and rule.

## Rule reference [#rule-reference]

Each entry says what the rule catches and what to do instead. The anchor of
each entry is the rule ID in lower case, for example
`analyzers.md#reactor_hooks_001`.

### Hooks [#hooks]

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_001 [#reactor_hooks_001]

A hook is called inside an `if`, a loop, a `switch`, or a lambda. Reactor
matches hooks by call order, so the order must be the same on every render.
Call the hook every time and branch on its result.

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_002 [#reactor_hooks_002]

A hook comes after an early `return`. On renders that return early, the
hooks below it are skipped and the order breaks. Move every hook above the
first `return`.

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_003 [#reactor_hooks_003]

The `UseEffect` lambda is `async`, so it compiles as `async void`.
Exceptions escape, the cleanup does not wait for the work, and a setter can
run after the component unmounts. Move the async work into a method and
start it from a normal effect. The code fix does this.

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_004 [#reactor_hooks_004]

A hook dependency is a new object, such as an array or a lambda, on every
render. It never equals the previous value, so the hook runs every time.
Wrap it in `UseMemo`, move it to a field, or pass a simple value instead.

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_005 [#reactor_hooks_005]

A hook is called outside `Render` or a custom hook. Only call hooks from a
`Render` override or from a method whose name starts with `Use`.

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_006 [#reactor_hooks_006]

A resource fetcher calls something that looks like a write. Resources run
again when their dependencies change, on retry, and on focus. Use
`UseMutation` for writes. See [Async resources](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/async-resources).

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_007 [#reactor_hooks_007]

The builder passed to `UseMemoCells`, `UseMemoCellsByKey`, or
`UseMemoCellsByIndex` uses a value that is not in its dependency list. The
cell does not update when that value changes. Add the value to the
dependencies.

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_008 [#reactor_hooks_008]

A state variable is read right after its setter in the same handler. The
setter only schedules a new render, so the variable still has the old value.
Use the value you passed to the setter.

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_009 [#reactor_hooks_009]

A `Command` sets `DebounceMs`, but it is not created with `UseCommand`. The
debounce state lives in that hook, so the command does not debounce. Create
it with `UseCommand(...)`. See [Commanding](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/commanding).

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_010 [#reactor_hooks_010]

An object or collection is changed in place, and the same instance is
passed back to its setter. The setter sees an equal value and does not
re-render. Pass a new instance, for example with a `with` expression or a
copy of the list.

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_011 [#reactor_hooks_011]

An input such as a `TextBox` shows a value from state, but its change
callback is empty or ignores the new value. The user's edits are lost.
Update state in the callback, or make the control read-only.

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_012 [#reactor_hooks_012]

A `Memo` dependency is a new object on every render, so the memo never
reuses its result. Make it stable with `UseMemo` or a field, or pass a
simple key.

#### REACTOR_HOOKS_013 [#reactor_hooks_013]

The initial value of `UseState` or `UsePersisted` allocates a new object on
every render, but the hook only reads it once. Wrap it in
`UseMemo(() => ..., [])`.

### State and context [#state-and-context]

#### REACTOR_STATE_001 [#reactor_state_001]

A component implements `INotifyPropertyChanged`. Reactor never listens to
it, so raising `PropertyChanged` does nothing. Keep state in `UseState`, or
use one of the observable bridges in [State management](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/data-system).

#### REACTOR_CTX_001 [#reactor_ctx_001]

A context value is a new object on every render, so every component that
reads the context re-renders. Wrap the value in `UseMemo`. See
[Context](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/context).

#### REACTOR_PERSIST_001 [#reactor_persist_001]

`UsePersisted` is called without a scope, so it uses
`PersistedScope.Application` and is shared by every window. Pass
`PersistedScope.Window` or `PersistedScope.Application` so the scope is
clear. See [Persistence](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/persistence).

### Lists and keys [#lists-and-keys]

#### REACTOR_DSL_001 [#reactor_dsl_001]

An item built in a dynamic list has no `.WithKey(...)`. The reconciler
matches rows by position, so an insert or a reorder re-creates the rows and
loses focus and state. Add a key from the item's ID.

#### REACTOR_DSL_002 [#reactor_dsl_002]

`.WithKey(...)` uses the list index, or a value such as `Guid.NewGuid()`
or `DateTime.Now`. These keys change when the list changes, so the rows are
re-created. Use the item's ID.

#### REACTOR_DSL_003 [#reactor_dsl_003]

A key selector, for example in a typed `ListView<T>`, ignores its item and
returns the same key for every item. Return a unique key for each item,
such as `item.Id`.

#### REACTOR_DSL_004 [#reactor_dsl_004]

The item implements `IReactorKeyed`, so `ForEach` already keys it. The
`.WithKey(...)` call repeats that key and can be removed.

#### REACTOR_ITEMS_001 [#reactor_items_001]

`.Set(...)` assigns `ItemsSource` on a collection element that Reactor
fills itself. This fights the keyed diff. Pass the data through the
element's `items` argument. See [Collections](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/collections).

#### REACTOR_ITEMS_002 [#reactor_items_002]

An `ItemsView` view builder returns something other than an
`ItemContainer`. `ItemsView` needs an `ItemContainer` root. The code fix
wraps the result in `ItemContainer(...)`.

#### REACTOR_MEMO_001 [#reactor_memo_001]

A modifier is applied to a keyed `Memo(key, factory)` wrapper. A wrapper
with modifiers can't use the cache that virtualized lists use when they
recycle rows. Move the modifiers inside the factory.

### Modifiers and .Set [#modifiers-and-set]

#### REACTOR_MOD_001 [#reactor_mod_001]

A placement modifier, such as `.Grid(...)` or `.Canvas(...)`, is applied
more than once in one chain. The last call replaces the earlier ones. Merge
them into one call.

#### REACTOR_MOD_002 [#reactor_mod_002]

`.Set(...)` writes a property that has a Reactor modifier. `.Set` runs on
every render and is never undone. Use the modifier instead.

#### REACTOR_MOD_003 [#reactor_mod_003]

The modifier does nothing on this control type. For example, `.Background`
has no effect on a `Rectangle`, because shapes use `.Fill`. Use the
modifier that the control supports.

#### REACTOR_PERF_001 [#reactor_perf_001]

`.Width(...)` and `.Height(...)` are chained on a built-in element. Each call
copies the element, so one `.Size(width: ..., height: ...)` call saves a copy.
The code fix makes the change and keeps the arguments in their original
order. This is a small allocation saving, not a bug. See
[Analyzer architecture](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/analyzer-architecture#combined-sizing-without-extra-copies).

#### REACTOR_POOL_001 [#reactor_pool_001]

`.Set(...)` writes a property that Reactor resets when it returns the
control to the pool. The value is lost on a later render. Use the matching
modifier. See [Element pooling](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/element-pool).

#### REACTOR_VIS_001 [#reactor_vis_001]

`.Set(c => c.Visibility = ...)` is not tracked, so the value is lost on the
next render or when the control is reused. Use `.IsVisible(bool)`.

#### REACTOR_EVENT_001 [#reactor_event_001]

An event is subscribed inside `.Set(...)`, which runs on every render and
adds a new handler each time. Use the event modifier if there is one.
Otherwise, subscribe in `.OnMountAdd(...)` and unsubscribe in
`.OnUnmountAdd(...)`.

### Controls and selection [#controls-and-selection]

#### REACTOR_CTRL_001 [#reactor_ctrl_001]

The control's selection is controlled by `SelectedIndex`, and
`.Set(x => x.SelectedItem = ...)` sets it a second way. The two fight.
Remove the `.Set(...)` call.

#### REACTOR_OPT_001 [#reactor_opt_001]

A selection property of type `Optional<T>` gets a sentinel value such as
`-1`. That forces the value on every render. Use `Optional<T>.Unset` to let
the control own the selection.

#### REACTOR_CMD_001 [#reactor_cmd_001]

An element sets both `Command` and its own callback, such as `OnClick`.
Reactor runs the callback, so the command never runs. Remove one of them.
See [Commanding](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/commanding).

#### REACTOR_PERF_FUNCREF [#reactor_perf_funcref]

A `new Command { ... }` is created in `Render` on every render. Wrap it in
`UseMemo(() => new Command { ... }, deps)` to keep one instance. The code
fix does this and works out the dependencies.

#### REACTOR_INPUT_001 [#reactor_input_001]

`.OnKeyDown` checks for a Ctrl or Alt shortcut. `.OnKeyDown` only runs while
the element has focus, so the shortcut doesn't work elsewhere. Register a
command with an accelerator instead. See
[Input and gestures](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/input-and-gestures).

#### REACTOR_INPUT_002 [#reactor_input_002]

A drop handler calls `TryGetFiles`, which can return network paths, device
paths, links, and virtual files from the drag source. Use
`TryGetSafeLocalFiles` to keep only safe local files.

### Theming [#theming]

#### REACTOR_THEME_001 [#reactor_theme_001]

A color is hard-coded, for example `"#0078D4"`. It does not change with the
light, dark, or high-contrast theme. Use a `Theme` token, such as
`Theme.Accent`. See [Theming tokens](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/theming-tokens).

#### REACTOR_THEME_002 [#reactor_theme_002]

`.Set(...)` writes a control property that also has a lightweight styling
resource key. The hover and pressed states keep their own colors. Set the
resource with `.Resources(r => r.Set(...))` instead.

#### REACTOR_THEME_003 [#reactor_theme_003]

`RequestedTheme` is set through `.Set(...)`. Use the
`.RequestedTheme(...)` modifier.

#### REACTOR_THEME_004 [#reactor_theme_004]

A brush, such as `new SolidColorBrush(Colors.White)`, is created inline. It
does not follow the theme. Use a `Theme` token.

### Accessibility [#accessibility]

#### REACTOR_A11Y_001 [#reactor_a11y_001]

A button shows only an icon or an element, not text. Screen readers can't
announce it. Add `.AutomationName("...")`. See
[Accessibility](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/accessibility).

#### REACTOR_A11Y_002 [#reactor_a11y_002]

An image has no accessible name. Add `.AutomationName("...")` as alt text,
or `.AccessibilityHidden()` if the image is only decoration.

#### REACTOR_A11Y_003 [#reactor_a11y_003]

A form field has no label. Add a `header:` argument, `.Header(...)`,
`.AutomationName(...)`, or `.LabeledBy(...)`.

#### REACTOR_A11Y_004 [#reactor_a11y_004]

A container has `.OnTapped(...)` but is not a tab stop, so keyboard users
can't reach it. Add `.IsTabStop(true)`, and handle Enter and Space in
`.OnKeyDown(...)`.

### Did you mean [#did-you-mean]

These rules catch names and arguments that are close to a real Reactor
API, usually typed by a person or an AI agent that guessed.

#### REACTOR_DYM_001 [#reactor_dym_001]

A Reactor property is called with parentheses, as if it were a method.
Remove the parentheses.

#### REACTOR_DYM_002 [#reactor_dym_002]

The `Theme` background token does not exist. The message names the token
you probably meant.

#### REACTOR_DYM_003 [#reactor_dym_003]

The name is not defined, but it is close to a Reactor factory name. The
message and the code fix suggest the factory.

#### REACTOR_DYM_004 [#reactor_dym_004]

A factory call is missing a required argument. The message shows the call
with the argument added.

#### REACTOR_DYM_005 [#reactor_dym_005]

A factory expects an element, but you passed a string. Wrap the string in a
text factory such as `TextBlock(...)`.

#### REACTOR_DYM_006 [#reactor_dym_006]

A color string, such as `"orange"`, is not a format Reactor can read, so the
color renders gray. The message suggests a hex value. Better still, use a
`Theme` token.

### Animation [#animation]

#### REACTOR_ANIM_002 [#reactor_anim_002]

The trigger passed to `.Keyframes(...)` changes on every render, so the
animation restarts each time and flickers. Pass a value that changes only
when you want to replay it, such as a counter in state. See
[Animation](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/animation).

#### REACTOR_ANIM_003 [#reactor_anim_003]

An `async` lambda is passed to `WithAnimation`. Changes after the first
`await` are not animated. Use one `WithAnimation` call for each step, around
each `await`.

#### REACTOR_ANIM_004 [#reactor_anim_004]

`.Set(...)` or `.OnMount(...)` writes `Rotation`, `Scale`, `CenterPoint`,
`RotationAxis`, `TransformMatrix` or a `*Transition` property, or calls
`StartAnimation`, on an element whose modifiers already own its composition
visual, such as `.Scale(...)`, `.Rotation(...)` or `.Keyframes(...)`. WinUI
rejects the write. Use the matching modifier, such as `.Rotation(...)` or
`.OpacityTransition()`; the code fix rewrites the simple cases. The rule also
flags a `.Set` that writes `Translation` on an element that uses
`.Translation(...)`. See [Animation](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/animation).

### Layout and media [#layout-and-media]

#### REACTOR_GRID_001 [#reactor_grid_001]

A `Grid` declares a row or column that no child is placed in. Remove the
track, or place a child in it. See [Layout](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/layout).

#### REACTOR_MEDIA_001 [#reactor_media_001]

A `WebView2` is a direct child of a stack and has no `.Width` and
`.Height`. It sizes itself to the page and keeps changing size. Set
`.Width` and `.Height`, or put it in a fixed-size grid cell.

### Lifecycle and threading [#lifecycle-and-threading]

#### REACTOR_LIFECYCLE_002 [#reactor_lifecycle_002]

A `UseEffect` creates a long-lived object, such as a timer or a
subscription, and returns no cleanup. It keeps running after the component
unmounts. Return a cleanup action that disposes it. See
[Effects](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/effects).

#### REACTOR_DIALOG_001 [#reactor_dialog_001]

`ContentDialog.ShowAsync()` opens a dialog outside the Reactor tree. Use the
`ContentDialog(...)` element with `IsOpen` instead. See
[Dialogs and flyouts](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/dialogs-and-flyouts).

#### REACTOR_NAV_001 [#reactor_nav_001]

A `UseNavigation` handle is stored in a static field or property. It
outlives the page and holds on to its dispatcher. Read it with
`UseNavigation<TRoute>()` where you need it, or pass it through context.

#### REACTOR_THREAD_001 [#reactor_thread_001]

A member that must run on the UI thread is called inside a background task.
Move the call back to the UI thread with
`ReactorApp.UIDispatcher?.TryEnqueue(...)`. See
[Threading and dispatch](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/threading-and-dispatch).

#### REACTOR_THREAD_002 [#reactor_thread_002]

`Render` or an effect blocks on a task, for example with `.Result` or
`.Wait()`. That freezes the UI. Use `UseResource`, or `await` inside an
effect.

### Advanced features [#advanced-features]

#### REACTOR_DOCK_001 [#reactor_dock_001]

`OnLiveLayoutChanged` passes the live dock layout straight into a setter.
The dock host already owns that layout, so writing it back breaks drag,
tab, and splitter behavior. Only read the layout in this callback. See
[Docking](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/docking).

#### REACTOR_ICON_001 [#reactor_icon_001]

A `WindowIcon` is passed to a surface that can't use its kind. For example,
the tray icon can't read a `FromResource` icon. The icon is dropped at run
time. The message names the kind to use instead.

#### REACTOR_WIN2D_001 [#reactor_win2d_001]

A Win2D canvas draws resources from `UseCanvasResources`, which live on the
shared device, but the canvas does not call `.UseSharedDevice()`.
This crashes at run time. Add `.UseSharedDevice()` to the canvas. See
[Win2D canvas](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/controls/win2d-canvas).

### Custom controls [#custom-controls]

These rules apply when you write your own control descriptors or handlers.
See [Extending Reactor controls](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/how-it-works/extending-reactor-controls).

#### REACTOR0050 [#reactor0050]

A OneWay descriptor entry uses `Optional<T>` but has no `dp:` argument.
Without the dependency property, `Unset` skips the write instead of clearing
the value. Add `dp:`. This is the only rule with a help link today. It
points to
[spec 050](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-ui-reactor/blob/main/docs/specs/050-controlled-prop-authority-and-optional-t.md).

#### REACTOR_DESC_001 [#reactor_desc_001]

The handler factory passed to `ControlRegistry.Register` is not a `static`
lambda. Mark it `static`, and move any captured state out, so trimming and
[Native AOT](/microsoft-ui-reactor/main/guides/native-aot) stay safe.

#### REACTOR_REF_001 [#reactor_ref_001]

`ElementRef.Current` is read to set a reference property. That value is a
snapshot, so it breaks when the target mounts late or unmounts. Declare the
reference through `descriptor.Reference` or `binding.Reference`.

#### REACTOR_LIFECYCLE_003 [#reactor_lifecycle_003]

A handler calls `Reconciler.UpdateChild`, which does not check that the
child's element type is the same, and does not unmount a control it
replaces. Call `Reconcile` and install its result when it differs from the
current control.

## Tips [#tips]

- Treat analyzer warnings as real bugs. Most of them point at code that
  compiles but behaves wrongly at run time.
- In CI, set `TreatWarningsAsErrors`, or run
  `mur check -- -p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`, so new warnings fail the
  build. `mur check --strict` shows every warning but keeps the build's exit
  code.
- Info-level rules don't fail a build. Run `mur check --final` before you
  merge to see them.
- If a rule is wrong for your code, turn it off for that line with
  `#pragma`, not for the whole project.
